title: An invertible projection formula forces coproduct preservation
statement: Let C and D be monoidal closed categories and suppose C has zero morphisms. Let I be a set for which C and D have all I-indexed coproducts. Let F : D → C preserve these coproducts and let F(1_D) be isomorphic to 1_C. Let G : C → D be a functor equipped with a natural bifunctor isomorphism G(M) ⊗ N ≅ G(M ⊗ F(N)). Then G preserves all I-indexed coproducts. No adjunction, additivity of G, or compatibility of the specified unit isomorphism with F is needed.

source.place: Categorical projection-formula argument written by V3, followed by the proved copower retract theorem

proof.text: For fixed M in C let Q be F followed by left tensoring with M. Tensoring preserves coproducts because the monoidal categories are closed; therefore Q preserves coproducts. The bifunctor projection isomorphism identifies Q followed by G with left tensoring by G(M), so Q followed by G also preserves coproducts.

Take the I-indexed coproduct cocone on the constant family of units in D. Q sends this to a colimit cocone, and Q followed by G also sends it to a colimit cocone. Thus G preserves the colimit of the diagram Q(unit).

The given unit isomorphism and the right unitor identify Q(unit) = M tensor F(unit) with M. Transport preservation along this constant-diagram isomorphism. Hence G preserves every I-indexed copower of every M.
Apply the copower retract theorem to conclude that G preserves arbitrary I-indexed coproducts. Its use of zero morphisms is only in C. Empty families are included.
